summary: William Hay Macnaghten was an Indologist. He studied at Charterhouse School from around 1805 to 1809 and later at Fort William College in 1816.
William Henry Carmichael Smyth worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Charterhouse School and later served as Resident Superintendent at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1822 to 1824.

William Henry Coxe studied Classics and Sanskrit at Balliol College, Oxford in 1858. An Indology and linguistics scholar, he worked as an Assistant at the British Museum (1861-1865) and briefly held the unpaid chair of Sanskrit at King's College London in 1865.
William Henry Fox Talbot was active in history, archaeology, and other fields. He completed his education at Harrow School until 1815 and then studied at Trinity College, Cambridge from 1817 to 1821.
William Henry Hale was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He earned a B.A. (~1856-1860) and a Ph.D. (~1860-1863) at Yale University, and completed an LL.B. at Albany Law School (~1860-1861).

William Henry Harris studied at Southern Nazarene University, Boston University, and at the University of Madras under T. M. P. Mahadevan. A philosophy and religious studies scholar, he taught at the University of Arkansas and Southern Illinois University Edwardsville.

William Henry Mill was an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge. He served as Principal of Bishop's College, Calcutta (1820-1838), and at Cambridge as Christian Advocate (1840) and Regius Professor of Hebrew (1848).

William Henry Sleeman was an Indology and history scholar. He served in the Bengal Army (1809-1854), was General Superintendent of the Thuggee and Dacoity Department (1835), and served as Resident at the University of Lucknow (1849-1856).
William Henry Sykes was an Indology and history scholar. He founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai and served as President of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1858.

William Henry Wait was a linguistics and Indology scholar. Educated at Northwestern, Allegheny College, Berlin, and Bonn, he taught at Illinois Wesleyan University and later at the University of Michigan as Professor of Modern Languages (~1895-1925).

William Hoey was an Indology and history scholar who earned his M.A. from Queen's University Belfast. He held posts as Reader in Hindustani and Indian History at the University of Oxford (~1906-1919) and Trinity College Dublin (1910).

William Holme Williams was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (A.B. 1876). He spent his career there, culminating as Professor of Semitic Languages and Hellenistic Greek from 1892 to 1917.
William Homan Thorpe studied at Jesus College, Cambridge (~1921-1924) and subsequently held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1932 to 1969, where he taught John Hurrell Crook.

William Hook Morley worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. Called to the bar at the Middle Temple in 1840, he later served as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland in 1859.

William Howard Campbell was a linguistics and Indology scholar. He earned an M.A. and B.D. at the University of Edinburgh (~1877-1882) and served as a missionary with the London Missionary Society from 1884 to 1903.
William Hoyles Drew was an Indologist who studied under the traditional teacher Ramanujan. He served as chaplain of the Madras Chapel for the London Missionary Society from 1834 to 1856.

William Hunter studied at Aberdeen. Working in Indology and linguistics, he was a surgeon at the Agra Residency (~1794-1803), Secretary of The Asiatic Society (1798-1811), and Examiner in Persian and Hindustani at Fort William College (1805-1811).
William Irvine was an Indology and history scholar who studied at King's College London (~1861-1862). He served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1864 to 1888.

William J. Gedney was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. under Franklin Edgerton at Yale University. He held posts at Cornell University, as Professor of Linguistics at the University of Ceylon, and at the University of Michigan (1960-1981).

William James was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Plymouth College and Harvard. He spent his academic career teaching at Harvard University from 1872, becoming full professor in 1885, and taught students including George Santayana.
